# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 16 (LOGOS Formal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 16
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Furthermore, I will also speak with you about the temple — how those wretched people were led astray and set their hope on a building as if it were the house of God, rather than on God himself who made them.
2. For they consecrated him in a temple almost as the Gentiles do. But what does the Lord say? "Who has measured the heaven with a span, or the earth with the palm of the hand? Have not I?" says the Lord. "Heaven is my throne and earth is my footstool: what sort of house will you build for me, and what place is for my rest?" says the Lord. You know therefore that their hope is vain.
3. Furthermore he says again: "Behold, those who tore down this temple will themselves build it."
4. It is coming to pass. For it was torn down by their enemies through war; and now the very servants of those enemies will rebuild it.
5. Again, it was revealed that the city and the temple and the people of Israel were to be given over. For the scripture says: "And it shall come to pass in the last days that the Lord shall give up the sheep of the pasture and the fold and the watchtower to destruction." And it came about as the Lord spoke.
6. Let us inquire then whether there is a temple of God. Indeed there is — in the place where he himself says he makes it and brings it to completion. For it is written: "And it shall come to pass when the week is ended that a temple of God will be built gloriously in the name of the Lord."
7. I find therefore that there is indeed a temple. How then shall it be built in the name of the Lord? Learn: before we believed in God, the dwelling of our heart was corrupt and weak, truly a house built by human hands — for it was full of idolatry and was a dwelling of demons, since we did everything that was contrary to God.
8. But it shall be built in the name of the Lord. Pay heed, so that the temple of the Lord may be built gloriously. How? Learn: having received the forgiveness of sins, and having set our hope on the Name, we became new — created anew from the beginning; and so God truly dwells in our dwelling place, that is, in us.
9. How? His word of faith, the calling of his promise, the wisdom of his righteous ordinances, the commandments of his teaching, himself prophesying in us, himself dwelling in us — opening to us who were enslaved to death the door of the temple, which is the mouth, giving us repentance, and leading us into the incorruptible temple.
10. For the one who desires to be saved looks not at the human being but at him who dwells in him and speaks through him, marveling that they never before heard these words from the mouth of the speaker, nor desired to hear them. This is a spiritual temple being built for the Lord.
